tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: List Air Automations visible to you — personal ones first, then project ones. Returns id, name, repository, projectId and a webUrl that opens it in the Air web UI, so linking needs no second call. Start here: the ids, projectId and repository shapes other tools need all come from this.

tools.name: get_automation
tools.description: Fetch one automation in full: prompt, triggers, triggerVcs, environmentConfigId, agentAndModel, projectId, plus webUrl to open it in the Air web UI. Use this to copy environmentConfigId and agentAndModel into a new automation, and always before update_automation.

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create a new Air Automation. Provide the complete spec. environmentConfigId is required — an automation without it has no secrets and no domain allowlist. Take repository, agentAndModel and projectId from an existing automation (list_automations, then get_automation). environmentConfigId comes from the same place, or from air-cloud's list_environments / create_environment when the repo has no automation yet.

prompt.description: The instruction the agent follows. Keeping it as a pointer to a file in the repo ("Read AUTOMATION_PROMPT.md and follow it") lets you version the real prompt in git.

repository.description: The repository the automation runs against. Copy it from an existing automation on the same repo via get_automation.

projectId.description: Omit for a personal (PRIVATE) automation; set it to share with a project. Get it from list_automations. Re-sharing works: an automation can be moved from one project to another any number of times. Going back to personal cannot be expressed at all — an empty string is a 400, null makes the backend's project permission check fail with a misleading 503, and omitting the key keeps the current project rather than clearing it. To make a shared automation personal again, delete it and create a new one without projectId.

agentAndModel.description: Cloud agent + model. Copy from an existing automation via get_automation — the catalog is not exposed here.

anyOf.description: Fires only when something POSTs to the automation

filters.description: ANDed exact/substring matches. No globs, ranges, OR or NOT.

items.description: EVENT triggers cannot use push-to-new-branch — only create-pr/read-only (youtrack, jira, non-PR github) or push-to-source/read-only (github pull_request.*). Use SCHEDULED or WEBHOOK if you need an enforced branch destination.

outputBehaviour.description: Where the agent may write. Not all values are available on every trigger type — see the triggers field.

items.description: Omit to accept the trigger type's default (push-to-new-branch for SCHEDULED, read-only for WEBHOOK).

environmentConfigId.description: Required as a field, but may be null — you must choose, not omit. An id attaches an environment configuration: secrets, allowlisted domains, VM size, startup script. This server cannot create or look up environments — air-cloud does: list_environments (filter by repositoryUrl) resolves a name to this id, create_environment makes one with variables, secrets and allowlist and returns it. Both see personal environments only; a project-owned one comes from get_automation on an automation that already uses it. Pass null only when the automation genuinely needs none of that (a read-only run on a public repo). A null here is the difference between a working automation and one that fails at run time with no credentials.

tools.name: update_automation
tools.description: Change an existing automation. The backend replaces the whole spec, so this tool reads the current one first and merges your fields over it — that keeps environmentConfigId and triggerVcs from being reset. triggers and triggerVcs pair by position, so pass both together or neither — changing one alone would move each destination onto a different trigger, and this tool refuses it. Only the automation's creator may update it. Saved as a new snapshot version.

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.description: Delete an automation permanently. confirmName must equal the automation's current name — fetch it with get_automation first. Only the creator may delete.

confirmName.description: The exact current name, as a guard against deleting the wrong one

tools.name: run_automation
tools.description: Start a run of an automation now, whatever its trigger type — the same as "Run now" in the Air web UI. Returns runId and statusUrl (the run page in the Air web UI). outputBehaviour is required because a manual run does NOT inherit the automation's triggerVcs: left to the platform it pushes to a new branch. Use "read-only" for a smoke test. Runs even when the automation is paused.

outputBehaviour.description: Where this run may write. "read-only" to verify an automation without touching the repo.

sourceBranch.description: Branch to check out for this run; defaults to the automation's branch

payload.description: Extra JSON handed to the run as its trigger context, like a webhook body

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Run history of an automation, newest first: runId, status, triggerSource, createdAt, errorMessage. status is lifecycle only — FINISHED means the agent stopped, not that the work succeeded. Read the outcome with get_run.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: One run in full, with what the agent reported: result.summary is the agent's closing message (markdown) and result.links what it linked to — this, not status, says whether the work succeeded. Empty while the run is going. For the step-by-step transcript (commands, exit codes, where it failed), pass sessionId to air-cloud's get_task_transcript.

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: Stop an active automation run by runId — the one run_automation returned. Same as Stop in the Air web UI; the run ends as CANCELLED.

tools.name: launch_task
tools.description: Launches a new AIR Cloud task: clones the given repository at the given ref and runs a coding agent there with the given prompt. Returns the new task's id and status.

repositoryUrl.description: The Git clone URL of the repository to launch the task in.

ref.description: The branch or commit ref to check out.

agentId.description: The coding agent to run, e.g. "claude".

prompt.description: The instructions for the agent to carry out.

model.description: Optional model name to use with the agent.

mode.description: Optional permission mode id to use from launch.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort id, e.g. low, medium, or high.

fast-mode.description: Whether to enable the agent's fast mode. Optional.

envConfigId.description: Optional id of the environment configuration to launch with; its repository must match repositoryUrl. When omitted, the caller's own configuration for the repository is used (the first by name), or the default one if there is none.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Lists AIR Cloud tasks visible to the caller, optionally filtered by repository.

repositoryUrl.description: Optional repository clone URL to filter tasks by.

offset.description: Number of items to skip (0-based). Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Gets a single AIR Cloud task by id.

taskId.description: The unique id of the task to fetch.

tools.name: get_task_transcript
tools.description: Fetches up to maxMessages newest ACP transcript messages for an AIR Cloud task or session, returned oldest first. Messages are parsed from JSON when possible.

taskId.description: AIR Cloud task id. Provide this or sessionId.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id. Provide this or taskId.

maxMessages.description: Maximum number of newest transcript messages to fetch. Defaults to 1000 and is capped at 5000.

tools.name: resume_task
tools.description: Resumes a suspended AIR Cloud task/session. Optionally queues a follow-up prompt through the Spawner resume API.

taskId.description: AIR Cloud task id. Provide this or sessionId.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id. Provide this or taskId.

prompt.description: Optional follow-up prompt to queue after the suspended session resumes.

model.description: Optional model name to use with the agent.

mode.description: Optional permission mode id to use from launch.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort id, e.g. low, medium, or high.

fast-mode.description: Whether to enable the agent's fast mode. Optional.

tools.name: archive_task
tools.description: Archives an AIR Cloud task and all of its sessions, retaining its history but preventing further use. An archived task cannot be resumed. Archiving an already archived task succeeds without changes.

taskId.description: The unique id of the task to archive.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Permanently deletes an AIR Cloud task and terminates all of its sessions. This cannot be undone.

taskId.description: The unique id of the task to permanently delete.

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Creates a personal AIR Cloud environment configuration: a repository plus environment variables, instance type and network policy that tasks can launch with. The response also lists the caller's own personal secrets on the configuration by name, with masked values (a freshly created configuration has none yet).

repositoryUrl.description: The Git clone URL of the repository this environment is for.

provider.description: Optional VCS provider of the repository: one of github, gitlab, space, bitbucket, github-enterprise, gitlab-self-managed. Stored so consumers need not infer it from the host; required to disambiguate self-hosted instances.

name.description: Optional environment name. Defaults to the repository name; if that name is already taken, a "-2", "-3", etc. suffix is appended.

variables.description: Environment variables to add or update. Existing variables not listed here are left as-is.

isSecret.description: Whether to store this value as a secret. Defaults to false.

instanceTypeKey.description: Optional instance type key to launch this environment on.

networkAccess.description: Network access mode: one of [UNRESTRICTED, RESTRICTED, DISABLED]. Defaults to RESTRICTED.

predefinedDomainLists.description: Predefined domain lists to allow when networkAccess is RESTRICTED: one or more of [WELL_KNOWN]. Defaults to [WELL_KNOWN].

allowedDomains.description: Additional domains to allow when networkAccess is RESTRICTED.

exposedPorts.description: Workspace ports to expose, as integers. Omit, set to null, or pass an empty list to expose none.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: Lists AIR Cloud environment configurations visible to the caller (owned or shared), optionally filtered by repository.

repositoryUrl.description: Optional repository clone URL to filter environments by.

includeDrafts.description: Whether to include in-progress draft environments. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_environment
tools.description: Gets a single AIR Cloud environment configuration by id, including its shared variables and the caller's own personal secrets on it, listed by name in `personalSecrets` (secret values are masked in both).

id.description: The unique id of the environment configuration to fetch.

tools.name: edit_environment
tools.description: Partially updates an AIR Cloud environment configuration: only the fields provided in the call are changed, everything else is left as-is. The response also lists the caller's own personal secrets on the configuration by name, with masked values.

id.description: The unique id of the environment configuration to edit.

variables.description: Environment variables to add or update. Existing variables not listed here are left as-is.

isSecret.description: Whether to store this value as a secret. Defaults to false.

instanceTypeKey.description: Optional instance type key to launch this environment on.

networkAccess.description: Network access mode: one of [UNRESTRICTED, RESTRICTED, DISABLED]. Defaults to RESTRICTED.

predefinedDomainLists.description: Predefined domain lists to allow when networkAccess is RESTRICTED: one or more of [WELL_KNOWN]. Defaults to [WELL_KNOWN].

allowedDomains.description: Additional domains to allow when networkAccess is RESTRICTED.

exposedPorts.description: Workspace ports to expose, as integers. Omit, set to null, or pass an empty list to expose none.

renames.description: Variables to rename, applied before any variables update.

tools.name: list_workflow_node_types
tools.description: Lists the built-in workflow node types (start, end, agentTask, humanTask, gateway, assign) and the JSON Schema of each one's config.

tools.name: list_workflow_templates
tools.description: Lists the built-in workflow templates (e.g. "review") that create_workflow can start a new workflow from.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: Lists workflow definitions in the caller's organization.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Gets a single workflow definition by id, including its full graph. The returned definition's 'problems' field lists executability issues; it must be empty before start_workflow.

tools.name: create_workflow
tools.description: Creates a new workflow definition, either from a built-in template, from a full graph, or (with neither) as a minimal start-to-end graph ready for authoring. The returned definition's 'problems' field lists executability issues; it must be empty before start_workflow.

templateId.description: Id of a built-in template to create the workflow from (see list_workflow_templates). Provide this or 'graph', not both.

graph.description: A full workflow graph ({agents, nodes, edges, inputSchema}) to create the workflow from. Provide this or 'templateId', not both. If neither is given, a minimal graph with only a start and end node is created.

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.description: Deletes a workflow definition while preserving its completed instance history. Fails if it still has running instances.

tools.name: set_workflow_agents
tools.description: Replaces the full list of agents declared on a workflow.

agents.description: Full replacement list of the workflow's declared agents.

items.description: A workflow agent: {id, name, agentId, modelId?, reasoningEffort?, envConfigId?, systemPrompt?, pushesResults?}. modelId is an exact catalog model id; reasoningEffort is a separate bare effort such as high or xhigh. pushesResults defaults to true and says whether this agent's work belongs on the instance's results branch; set it false for agents that only read the work, such as reviewers or steering agents.

tools.name: set_workflow_input_schema
tools.description: Sets or clears (with null) the JSON Schema a workflow's instance input must satisfy.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema the instance's input must satisfy, or null to clear it.

tools.name: add_workflow_step
tools.description: Adds a node to a workflow's graph, or replaces an existing node with the same id. The returned definition's 'problems' field lists executability issues; it must be empty before start_workflow.

step.description: A workflow node: {id, type, config?, ui?}. Replaces any existing node with the same id.

tools.name: update_workflow_step
tools.description: Replaces an existing node in a workflow's graph, matched by id.

step.description: A workflow node: {id, type, config?, ui?}. Replaces any existing node with the same id.

tools.name: remove_workflow_step
tools.description: Removes a node and any edges touching it from a workflow's graph.

stepId.description: Id of the node to remove, along with its edges.

tools.name: connect_workflow_steps
tools.description: Adds an edge between two nodes, or replaces an existing edge between the same pair. The returned definition's 'problems' field lists executability issues; it must be empty before start_workflow.

condition.description: Optional JSONata condition; an edge without one is the default.

tools.name: disconnect_workflow_steps
tools.description: Removes the edge between two nodes, if one exists.

tools.name: start_workflow
tools.description: Starts a new instance of a workflow definition against a repository checked out from the given environment configuration and ref.

workflowId.description: The workflow definition id to start an instance of.

input.description: Instance input, validated against the workflow's inputSchema.

envConfigId.description: Id of the environment configuration whose repository the instance runs against.

ref.description: Branch or commit ref to check out.

tools.name: list_workflow_instances
tools.description: Lists the workflow instances the caller started, optionally filtered by the workflow definition they were started from.

workflowId.description: Optional workflow definition id to filter instances by.

tools.name: get_workflow_instance
tools.description: Advances a workflow instance (ticks any pass-through nodes and launches pending steps) and returns its current state.

tools.name: cancel_workflow_instance
tools.description: Cancels a running workflow instance and any of its in-flight step runs.

tools.name: complete_workflow_step
tools.description: Completes a human-task step run that is waiting, with optional structured output.

stepRunId.description: The waiting step run id to complete.

output.description: Optional structured output for the step. Every field the node's outputSchema lists as required must be present.

tools.name: retry_workflow_step
tools.description: Retries a failed step run as a new iteration of the same node.

stepRunId.description: The failed step run id to retry.

tools.name: connect_task_agent
tools.description: Opens a live ACP connection to the coding agent of an AIR Cloud task so you can stream its updates and send follow-up messages. Provide either a taskId (resolved to its Agent Spawner session) or a sessionId directly. Idempotent: reconnecting an already-connected session is a no-op. Requires write permission.

taskId.description: AIR Cloud task id. Provide this or sessionId.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id. Provide this or taskId.

tools.name: send_task_message
tools.description: Sends one prompt turn to a connected task agent and waits for the turn to end, returning the final ACP stop reason. Streamed updates during the turn are buffered — read them with read_task_events using the returned cursor. Only one prompt may be in flight per session. Requires write permission.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id returned by connect_task_agent.

prompt.description: The message to send to the agent.

annotations.title: Send a message to a task agent

tools.name: read_task_events
tools.description: Reads buffered live events (streamed updates and lifecycle transitions) for a session, newest after the given cursor. Pass the returned cursor back to page forward; `dropped` signals the buffer evicted events you never read. Read-only.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id returned by connect_task_agent.

cursor.description: Return events with index greater than this. Omit or 0 to read from the start.

tools.name: cancel_task_message
tools.description: Cancels the in-flight prompt turn for a session, if any. Returns whether a turn was cancelled. Requires write permission.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id returned by connect_task_agent.

tools.name: disconnect_task_agent
tools.description: Closes the live ACP connection for a session, aborting any in-flight prompt and dropping its buffered events. Safe to call for an unknown session. Requires write permission.

sessionId.description: Agent Spawner session id returned by connect_task_agent.
